# RETRO: #12972 follow-up

## What worked
- Neutral shared brief with dependency sources named in scope. Both reviewers read inotify-tools source, and that is where the decisive N1 mechanism (commit 3e09f134) came from.
- Cross-examination changed the outcome twice. It independently confirmed N1 (Sol's initial report had missed the IN_ISDIR suppression), and it dropped a Sol finding (|| true hides failures) that kernel source contradicted. Neither reviewer was shown the other's conclusion.
- Opus ran a baseline-vs-head test and end-to-end timing. That gave concrete public numbers (305 attempts in 2s, 29.995s vs 0.107s).

## Friction / process deviations
- The coordinator's first packet read used a width projection (`cut -c1-400`), and a later read used `fold | head`. The full bodies were then read completely through JSON extraction. The dispatch message did not state the 60-line bound before the workflow reads. Policy reads used chunks of 50 lines or fewer, but some lines were very long.
- The 10-minute Sol status sleep fired after Sol had already exited (harmless).
- Editorial check 1 returned revise because "**Minor:**" read as a severity label. It was changed to "**Optional cleanup:**", and fresh check 2 passed.
- The version string of the installed inotify-tools cannot identify the release, because both tags carry 4.23.9.0. Behavior-based identification was used instead.

## Carry forward
- For inotify-based code, check the release-specific output filtering in inotifywait (src/inotifywait.cpp), not only the libinotifytools include matching.
- When a reviewer's claim rests on a kernel ABI, ask for the kernel source at a recorded tag early.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `711ec34a`, reassessing the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5791310535) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5797370017).

**Verified:** both earlier findings are resolved. One new, low-impact issue affects the new ancestor-directory fallback.

| Earlier finding | Status at `711ec34a` |
|---|---|
| Missing state directory causes immediate retries | **Resolved.** The watcher attaches to the closest existing parent, and a failed watch setup now backs off 5s. The PR's new test passes at this head and fails against the `411d128f` scripts (305 attempts in 2s). A real watcher with an always-failing `inotifywait` retried every 5.0s with no fd growth. |
| Unrelated device opens trigger camera rescans | **Resolved.** With `--include`, inotify-tools drops non-matching `/dev` child events before they reach the pipe. In a private directory stand-in, an unfiltered watcher reported `OPEN`/`CLOSE` of `null`; the filtered watcher did not, but still reported `video0` open, close and delete. Not measured on a live `/dev`; the CPU figures in the reply were not reproduced. |

**Verified:** the other claims in the reply hold in isolated runs. An event landing mid-scan was picked up on the next scan (3.3s) rather than after the 30s timeout (33.2s at `411d128f`). `|| true` keeps a camera that disappears mid-toggle from aborting the loop. Waiters do not accumulate fds or children, and all exit when the watcher is terminated. The new test stubs `inotifywait`, so it covers the back-off and the watch arguments, not the real event filtering.

### The ancestor watch does not wake when the flag directory is created

[`omarchy-camera-status:94-118`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/711ec34a39a73b1c4e2bb1a6ce20e98fbdcdfa15/bin/omarchy-camera-status#L94-L118) watches the closest existing parent and includes the flag directory in the `--include` regex, so that its creation should wake the loop. Since inotify-tools commit [`3e09f134`](https://github.com/inotify-tools/inotify-tools/commit/3e09f134d90789bee453d1db75968a3f424c9ec8) (in the 4.25.9.0 tag), `inotifywait` never prints directory (`IN_ISDIR`) events while an include filter is set, even when the path matches. The `inotifywait` used in testing behaves this way, although its help output reports `4.23.9.0`, which both tags carry.

```text
/var/lib/omarchy absent, watcher on /var/lib
  toggle off: mkdir /var/lib/omarchy        -> CREATE,ISDIR matches regex, dropped by inotifywait
              create camera-disabled inside -> not visible to the /var/lib watch
  loop wakes on the next /dev/video* event or the 30s read timeout
```

Isolated end-to-end run with the pinned script, a synthetic USB video interface and no `/dev/video*` change: `disabled: true` appeared after 30.0s with the directory missing, against 0.1s with it present. Both reviewers reproduced the dropped directory event separately in private directories, each with an unfiltered control.

**Impact:** limited to the first-ever disable on a system without `/var/lib/omarchy`. On a real toggle, deauthorizing a bound camera removes its `/dev/videoN` node, which does wake the loop, so a visible delay needs both conditions. Staleness is bounded by the 30s timeout. The code comment at lines 97-98 describes a wake-up that does not fire with this `inotifywait` behavior.

**Suggested change:** create `/var/lib/omarchy` ahead of time (for example in install or a migration) so the fallback is never needed. Alternatively, while the watch is on an ancestor, run a separate unfiltered `inotifywait -e create` on that directory writing to the same pipe. Neither approach was tested.

**Optional cleanup:** in [`omarchy-toggle-camera:69`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/711ec34a39a73b1c4e2bb1a6ce20e98fbdcdfa15/bin/omarchy-toggle-camera#L69) and [`:83`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/711ec34a39a73b1c4e2bb1a6ce20e98fbdcdfa15/bin/omarchy-toggle-camera#L83), `2>/dev/null` comes after `>"$interface/authorized"`. When the file is already gone, bash reports the failed open before stderr is redirected, so "No such file or directory" is still printed. Swapping the two redirections silences it; the `|| true` behavior is unaffected.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `411d128f..711ec34a` and the inotify-tools, bash, util-linux and Linux kernel sources involved, plus isolated command-level runs: the PR's shell test at both heads, the real watcher with a stubbed or real `inotifywait` in private directories, and synthetic USB interfaces. No live `/dev` workload, USB switching, udev, root toggle, PipeWire or desktop GUI. Suggested changes were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis; independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, each followed by one targeted follow-up question; Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
